standard_prerequisites.name: Signed tableau rules for quantifiers
standard_prerequisites.statement: From False (exists x A(x)) the False-exists rule derives False A(t); from True (forall x A(x)) the True-forall rule derives True A(t).
standard_prerequisites.use: Item (1) closes via the False-exists derivation against True A(t); item (2) closes via the True-forall derivation against False A(t).

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1267-1273): (1) A(t) proves exists x A(x); (2) forall x A(x) proves A(t).

Item prvEx (proof lines 1277-1283): a closed tableau for {False (exists x A(x)), True A(t)}: the False-exists rule applied to the root derives False A(t), which closes against the assumption True A(t).

Item prvAll (proof lines 1284-1292): a closed tableau for {False A(t), True (forall x A(x))}: the True-forall rule applied to the forall assumption derives True A(t), which closes against the assumption False A(t).
proof_roadmap: Witness prvEx with the False-exists derivation closing against True A(t).
Witness prvAll with the True-forall derivation closing against False A(t).
Both closed tableaux establish the two quantifier provability facts.
difficulty_reason: Quantifier provability facts (statement 1267-1273, proof 1275-1292): both closed-tableau constructions carried in span as tagitem branches, all node formulas in the standard two-argument form. H2.
